stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta:S\to\mathbf Z$. For any $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite type, write $\delta_T(t)=\delta(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$; for integral closed $W\subset T$, let $\dim_\delta W=\delta_T(\eta_W)$.

A $q$-cycle on $T$ is a locally finite integral linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $q$; $Z_q(T)$ is the group of these cycles. For a closed subscheme $W$ of dimension at most $q$, $[W]_q$ is the sum of the $q$-dimensional components weighted by generic-point length multiplicities. The Chow group $\mathrm{CH}_q(T)$ is $Z_q(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by locally finite principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $q+1$.

For a nonzero meromorphic section $u$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on an integral scheme $W$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal M}(u)$ is the Weil divisor with local coefficients given by the order of the representing meromorphic function in a trivialization at each codimension-one integral closed subscheme. Its Chow class is $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap[W]$. A global section $u$ has scheme-theoretic zero locus $Z(u)$. The operation $c_1(\mathcal M)\cap-:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(T)$ is defined by restriction to each integral component $W$ and proper pushforward to $T$, and descends to Chow groups.

For a flat morphism $h:T'\to T$ of relative dimension $r$, the flat pullback $h^*:Z_q(T)\to Z_{q+r}(T')$ sends $[W]$ to the cycle $[T'\times_TW]_{q+r}$ weighted by the lengths at generic points of components. It descends to Chow groups.

For a proper morphism $h:T'\to T$, the proper pushforward sends $[W]$ for integral closed $W$ of dimension $q$ to $[\kappa(\eta_W):\kappa(\eta_{h(W)})][h(W)]$ if the image has dimension $q$ and to zero if its dimension is smaller; this extends linearly to cycles and Chow groups.

For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal M$ on $T$ and section $u$, put $E=Z(u)$ with inclusion $j:E\hookrightarrow T$. The Gysin map $j^*:Z_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-1}(E)$ sends integral closed $[W]$ to $[E\cap W]_{q-1}$ if $W\not\subset E$, and to $(W\hookrightarrow E)_*(c_1(\mathcal M|_W)\cap[W])$ if $W\subset E$. Extend linearly. Under base change, the pulled-back section defines the corresponding Gysin map. This Gysin map descends to Chow groups.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ and integer $p$, a bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to Y)$ is a collection of homomorphisms $c_T:\mathrm{CH}_q(T)\to\mathrm{CH}_{q-p}(X\times_YT)$ indexed by $T\to Y$ and $q$, satisfying: (i) for proper $h:T'\to T$, $c_T(h_*\beta)=h_{X,*}c_{T'}(\beta)$; (ii) for flat $h$ of fixed relative dimension, $c_{T'}(h^*\alpha)=h_X^*c_T(\alpha)$; (iii) for $i:E\hookrightarrow T$ the zero scheme of a section of an invertible sheaf, $c_E(i^*\alpha)=i_X^*c_T(\alpha)$, with $h_X,i_X$ the base changes. Composition of families gives products $A^p(X\to Y)\times A^q(Y\to Z)\to A^{p+q}(X\to Z)$, and $A^*(X)=\bigoplus_pA^p(X\to X)$.

Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then the rule that to $f : X' \to X$ assigns
$c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \cap - : \mathrm{CH}_k(X') \to \mathrm{CH}_{k - 1}(X')$
is a bivariant class of degree $1$.

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $c_1(\mathcal{L}) \in A^1(X)$ is in the center of $A^*(X)$ and

then $c \circ c_1(\mathcal{L}) = c_1(f^*\mathcal{L}) \circ c$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $X$ be a
finite type scheme over $S$ which has an ample invertible sheaf.
Assume $d = \dim(X) < \infty$ (here we really mean dimension and
not $\delta$-dimension).
Then for any invertible sheaves $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_{d + 1}$
on $X$ we have
$c_1(\mathcal{L}_1) \circ \ldots \circ c_1(\mathcal{L}_{d + 1}) = 0$
in $A^{d + 1}(X)$.
